151: Hill elaborates on the LAW OF ECONOMICS, which was passed by Nature. There is no Supreme Court for appeals. The law hands out penalties and rewards without interference. It cannot be repealed—it is as fixed as the stars. One may refuse to adapt, but when large numbers join to ignore the law and take by force, THEN COMES THE DICTATOR, WITH WELL-ORGANIZED FIRING SQUADS AND MACHINE GUNS! America has never reached that stage. Hill predicts we shall prefer to continue with FREEDOM OF SPEECH, FREEDOM OF DEED, and FREEDOM TO RENDER USEFUL SERVICE IN RETURN FOR RICHES. He notes that government officials extending the privilege of raiding the public treasury for votes may win elections, but the final payoff comes when every penny wrongfully used must be repaid with compound interest. If the grabbers don't repay, the burden falls on their children 'even unto the third and fourth generations.' People can form groups to crowd wages up and hours down, but only to a point—where the LAW OF ECONOMICS steps in and the sheriff gets both employer and employees.
152: Hill reflects on the six years from 1929 to 1935 when America barely missed seeing 'Old Man Economics' hand over to the sheriff all businesses, industries, and banks. It was not a pretty sight and did not increase respect for mob psychology through which people cast reason aside and tried to GET WITHOUT GIVING. Those who went through those six discouraging years—when FEAR WAS IN THE SADDLE AND FAITH WAS ON THE GROUND—cannot forget how ruthlessly the LAW OF ECONOMICS exacted its toll from rich and poor, weak and strong, old and young. These observations come from 25 years of careful analysis of America's most successful individuals. These resourceful, hard-working, smart-thinking people represent the real genius of the American system. Their attributes helped the nation survive the Great Depression and flourish. One of those attributes is DEFINITENESS OF DECISION—the Seventh Step to Riches, to which Hill now turns. The page ends with the quote: 'God seems to throw Himself on the side of the individual who knows exactly what he wants, if he is determined to get JUST THAT!'

154: This page opens Chapter 7: DECISION—The Mastery of Procrastination (The Seventh Step to Riches). Hill states that analysis of thousands who failed revealed LACK OF DECISION near the head of the 30 Major Causes of Failure. PROCRASTINATION, the opposite of DECISION, is a common enemy everyone must conquer. Analysis of several hundred people who accumulated fortunes well beyond the million-dollar mark disclosed that every one had the habit of REACHING DECISIONS PROMPTLY and changing them slowly. People who fail to accumulate money have the habit of reaching decisions very slowly (if at all) and changing them quickly and often. Henry Ford's most outstanding quality was his habit of reaching decisions quickly and definitely, and changing them slowly—so pronounced it gave him the reputation of being obstinate. This quality prompted Ford to continue manufacturing the Model T (the world's ugliest car) when all advisors and many purchasers urged him to change it.
155: Hill acknowledges Ford perhaps delayed too long in changing the Model T, but the other side is that his firmness yielded a huge fortune before the change became necessary. Ford's definiteness of decision assumed the proportion of obstinacy, but this quality is preferable to slowness in reaching decisions and quickness in changing them. The majority who fail to accumulate money are easily influenced by others' opinions, permitting newspapers and gossiping neighbors to do their thinking. Opinions are the cheapest commodities on earth—everyone has a flock ready to impose. If influenced by others' opinions when reaching DECISIONS, you will not succeed in any undertaking. Keep your own counsel when putting these principles into practice. Take no one into confidence EXCEPT Master Mind Group members, choosing only those in COMPLETE SYMPATHY AND HARMONY with your purpose. Close friends and relatives, though well-meaning, often handicap one through opinions or ridicule. Thousands carry inferiority complexes because some ignorant person destroyed their confidence. You have a brain and mind of your own—USE THEM. If you need facts from others, acquire them quietly without disclosing your purpose. Those with smattering knowledge do TOO MUCH TALKING and TOO LITTLE LISTENING. Keep eyes and ears open and mouth CLOSED to acquire the habit of prompt DECISION.
